title: Ending an ACT tenancy
description: Steps for ending an ACT tenancy and releasing the bond. Summarised from act.gov.au renting pages and the ACT Revenue Office.

sources.title: When landlords can end a tenancy

items.title: Confirm you have a ground: you can't end a tenancy for no reason
For a fixed term, check it has ended or a breach, ACAT order or posting clause applies
Give the right notice: 8 weeks to sell or move in, 12 weeks for major renovations, 26 weeks for change of use
Attach proof such as a sales contract, statutory declaration or quotes
For a breach, give a notice to remedy before a notice to vacate
If the tenant doesn't leave, apply to ACAT
Do the final inspection with the tenant against the start condition report
Lodge the ACT bond refund form, with reasons and a repair estimate for any claim
If the tenant disputes your claim, it goes to ACAT
